title: Continuous differentials of a formal power-series quotient
statement: Let $F$ be a field, $n\ge0$, $D=F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $\mathfrak n=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\subset D$, and $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$ with each $f_j\in\mathfrak n$. Let $R=D/I$ and $\mathfrak n_R=\mathfrak nR$. Define the module of continuous $F$-differentials of $R$ as $\widehat\Omega_{R/F}=\varprojlim_r\Omega_{(R/\mathfrak n_R^r)/F}$ (Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], transition maps induced by the quotient maps), with the $F$-derivation $\widehat{\mathrm d}:R\to\widehat\Omega_{R/F}$, $x\mapsto(\mathrm d(x\bmod\mathfrak n_R^r))_r$. Then the $R$-linear map from the cokernel of $R^{\oplus s}\to R^{\oplus n}$, whose $j$-th column is $(\partial f_j/\partial t_i\bmod I)_i$, to $\widehat\Omega_{R/F}$ sending the class of the $i$-th basis vector $e_i$ to $\widehat{\mathrm d}(t_i\bmod I)$ is well defined and is an isomorphism.
